problem: Learnware specifications reveal capability-relevant information to identify helpful models, but risk exposing sensitive training data properties.
approach: Formalizes learnware-inversion as statistical decision games with risk measured as incremental Bayes value, deriving risk bounds for reduced kernel mean embedding specifications through RKHS-smoothed analysis.
contribution: First framework analyzing specification privacy risk in learnware, proving that properly-sized RKME specifications introduce negligible privacy risk while retaining sufficient identification information.

problem: Multimodal LLMs allow adversaries to distribute malicious intent across modalities to evade unimodal safeguards.
approach: Proposes FlowGuard, monitoring internal cross-modal consistency during multimodal fusion via Partial Information Decomposition to detect harmful inputs when text-only and vision-only reasoning diverge.
contribution: Reduces Attack Success Rates from >90% to <15% on unseen attacks with <3% utility loss and 6× latency reduction by detecting cross-modal fusion inconsistencies.

problem: Few-shot learning support sets quickly constructed with noise; even single noisy samples distort class distributions and reduce generalization in data-scarce settings.
approach: Detects noisy samples via low-rank anomalies in semantic feature space, then uses rank-guided diffusion to generate high-quality replacements under low-rank constraints.
contribution: Significantly reduces errors under noise levels up to 40% across MiniImageNet and TieredImageNet by mitigating prototype drift through low-rank geometry.

problem: Data selection for downstream tasks lacks theoretical grounding; existing methods treat valuation and selection separately without principled connection.
approach: Reformulates data selection as sequential decision-making where optimal sequences arise from dynamic programming; reinterprets existing methods like Data Shapley as myopic approximations.
contribution: Unifies existing data valuation methods through DP lens and proposes bipartite-graph surrogate enabling scalable greedy selection with provable guarantees.

problem: Model-based offline RL suffers from compounding errors during repeated model inference; geometric horizon models struggle with distant future state prediction.
approach: Introduces universal horizon models generalizing geometric horizon models to directly predict future states under arbitrary horizons with winsorized horizon distribution for training stability.
contribution: Outperforms competitive baselines on 100 OGBench tasks, particularly on highly suboptimal datasets requiring long-horizon reasoning.

problem: Private hypothesis selection requires either expensive exponential mechanism with pairwise comparisons or sub-optimal statistical rates.
approach: Designs score function based on small set of strong hypotheses enabling efficient evaluation without pairwise comparisons, reducing computational overhead significantly.
contribution: Achieves near-optimal statistical rates while running in nearly linear time in number of hypotheses under differential privacy constraints.

problem: LLM agents struggle with knowledge-intensive real-world optimization problems requiring domain expertise and appropriate mathematical techniques.
approach: Opt-Miner learns to identify missing knowledge, retrieve technical documents, and ground models via tree-guided data synthesis and retrieval-based group relative policy optimization.
contribution: Opt-Miner-Qwen3-8B achieves performance comparable to 32B specialized agents on complex multi-domain problems by active information seeking.

problem: Training coding agents specialized to private codebases is too costly and complex despite open-weight models' theoretical advantage.
approach: SERA generates thousands of synthetic trajectories via Soft Verified Generation without unit tests, then applies supervised finetuning on 200K+ synthetic trajectories.
contribution: 26x cheaper than RL and 57x cheaper than prior synthetic data methods while matching open-weight models; enables rapid creation of specialized agents.

problem: Learning factorial action policies from preference data ignores strategic interdependence; existing conjoint analyses average over opponent attributes.
approach: Learns stochastic interventions optimizing expected outcomes in average-case and minimax settings; extends to two-player adversarial selection capturing strategic simultaneous choice.
contribution: Adversarially-learned policies produce restricted-equilibrium vote shares aligning with historical election ranges, outperforming non-adversarial baselines.

problem: Why contrastive learning with simple images and augmentations yields useful representations for downstream tasks remains unexplained theoretically.
approach: Analytically computes optimal representations under contrastive loss for various augmentations; shows optimum attained by CNNs with sinusoid filters followed by nonlinearity and whitening.
contribution: Optimal weights form sinusoids whose frequencies can be computed via waterfilling algorithm; empirical CNNs trained with SGD learn these sinusoid patterns.

problem: Unknown transformations distort observations in machine learning and scientific modeling; recovering inverse transformations requires handling complex group structure.
approach: Models transformation posterior as Boltzmann distribution; introduces diffusion process on Lie groups with trivialized target-score identity enabling efficient sampling on-manifold.
contribution: TIED restores transformed inputs to training distribution at test time, improving robustness on image homographies and PDE symmetries over canonicalization baselines.

problem: Learning from label proportions with aggregate label information lacks low-variance debiasing methods supporting diverse loss functions.
approach: Introduces versatile low-variance debiasing methodology accommodating broad spectrum of practically relevant losses across binary and multi-class settings.
contribution: Improves sample complexity guarantees for large class of losses and validates empirical efficacy across diverse benchmarks over standard baselines.

problem: Irregular multivariate time series forecasting challenged by non-uniform sampling and asynchronicity violating equidistant assumptions of standard models.
approach: TFMixer uses learnable Non-Uniform Discrete Fourier Transform to extract spectral representations from irregular timestamps; fuses time and frequency domains.
contribution: Effectively forecasts irregular time series under non-uniform sampling and missing data; explicit seasonal extrapolation via inverse NUDFT.

problem: Robust RL under average-reward criterion lacks model-free algorithms with finite sample complexity analysis in data-limited scenarios.
approach: Proposes Robust Halpern Iteration with K-order multi-level Monte-Carlo estimator for accurate worst-case performance; instantiates for multiple uncertainty models.
contribution: Achieves ε-optimal robust policy with sample complexity of Õ(SAH²/ε^(2+o(1))) asymptotically matching best robust average-reward RL complexity.

problem: Grokking phenomenon where models suddenly generalize long after overfitting remains poorly understood mechanistically.
approach: Through mechanistic analysis finds grokking driven by structural reorganization of token representations; proposes R2G Loss enforcing repulsion on representation manifold.
contribution: R2G Loss enhances model efficiency via angular reorganization verified theoretically and empirically across algorithmic and linguistic tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLM architectures trade off training and inference efficiency; embedding space alignment is inference-inefficient while cross-attention is training-inefficient.
approach: NAEViT eliminates visual token attention interactions; SAISA aligns visual features with input spaces of attention blocks, reducing computational overhead in attention and FFNs.
contribution: SAISA achieves superior performance with significantly reduced computational costs across various baseline models, sizes, and training datasets.

problem: LLMs struggle detecting malicious behaviors fragmented across files when intricate dependencies are lost in vast amounts of benign code.
approach: Parses project into code graph, encodes nodes with semantic/structural signals, trains GNN under sparse supervision, guides LLM attention to identified key sections.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing approaches on multiple datasets while reducing interference from irrelevant context and maintaining low annotation costs.

problem: FFT-based pansharpening methods ignore spectral coordinate structure and radially-decaying energy distribution inherent in frequency-domain representations.
approach: Generalizes classical Butterworth filter into anisotropic learnable frequency-domain gating mechanism serving as efficient self-attention alternative.
contribution: ABFNet achieves state-of-the-art pansharpening performance with low computational overhead; superior CIFAR-100 classification validates broader applicability.

problem: Diffusion transformers for video generation suffer from prohibitive computational cost of spatiotemporal 3D full attention despite its quadratic complexity.
approach: DFSAttn provides training-free sparse attention with Hilbert curve token reordering for fine-grained sparsity, hierarchical block scoring, and adaptive sparse mask caching.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.1× end-to-end speedup while maintaining high generation quality under high sparsity ratios.

problem: Scaling LLM theorem provers challenged by training-time RL inefficiency and inference-time computational constraints on search.
approach: Multi-turn off-policy RL with expert iteration and adaptive filtering; planner-enhanced multi-agent system decomposes theorems hierarchically with proof cache sharing.
contribution: BFS-Prover-V2 achieves 95.08% on miniF2F and 41.4% on ProofNet test sets via scalable dual approach to training and inference.

problem: Federated learning for pathology deployment faces heterogeneity from diverse MIL architectures and heterogeneous feature extractors across institutions.
approach: FedHD performs local Gaussian-mixture feature alignment via distillation; generates synthetic counterparts for each slide to preserve diagnostic diversity.
contribution: Architecture-agnostic, privacy-preserving framework outperforms federated and distillation baselines on TCGA-IDH, CAMELYON16, CAMELYON17.

problem: NVIDIA's 2:4 Sparse Tensor Cores demand strict 50% pruning causing severe accuracy loss; milder patterns like 6:8 receive no hardware support.
approach: SlideSparse rewrites (2N-2):2N weight blocks into overlapping 2:4-compliant windows via Sliding Window Decomposition; fuses activation rearrangement into quantization.
contribution: 1.33× speedup matches theoretical upper-bound N/(N-1)=4/3 at 6:8 sparsity; enables better accuracy-speedup tradeoffs for LLM acceleration.

problem: Embodied agents need skill grounding across different embodiments and environments but LLMs impractical while small LMs insufficient for effective grounding.
approach: RECENT decouples skill semantics from embodiment-specific execution binding via code refactoring; modifies execution bindings rather than regenerating code.
contribution: Achieves best sLM-based Code-as-Policies performance matching LLM-based CaP across diverse robot embodiments in dynamic environments.

problem: Continuous-time event-native SNNs impose inherently sequential spike processing and require precise spike times without time bins, hindering practical training.
approach: Uses parallel associative scans to consume multiple spikes concurrently with exact hard-reset dynamics; implements differentiable spike time solvers to machine precision.
contribution: Yields up to 44× speedups over sequential simulation while retaining exact dynamics; enables end-to-end training on event-based datasets on GPUs.

problem: Existing evaluation systems neither capture human-in-the-loop coding nor adequately measure AI-human collaboration value.
approach: CentaurEval introduces Collaboration-Necessary templates intractable for standalone LLMs or humans but solvable through effective collaboration.
contribution: While LLMs/humans alone achieve poor rates (0.67% and 18.89%), human-AI collaboration improves to 31.11% under strategic intervention.

problem: Computing optimal k-query quantum ordered search beyond k=6 intractable; existing solvers require explicit large constraint matrices.
approach: Introduces matrix-free GPU SDP framework evaluating structured OSP constraints on-the-fly via custom CUDA kernels reducing memory from quadratic to linear.
contribution: Provides strong evidence k=6 optimal list size ≥90,000, improving query coefficient from 0.390 to 0.365; rigorously certifies N* < 94,000.

problem: 3D molecule generation via transformers challenged by SE(3)-equivariance requirements and permutation invariance plus continuous 3D coordinate modeling.
approach: InertialAR performs generation-oriented canonical tokenization via inertial frames; proposes geometric positional encoding enabling 3D geometric awareness in attention.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on 8/10 metrics for unconditional generation; significantly outperforms on controllable generation for targeted chemical functionality.

problem: Data diversity measured via text metrics provides weak signals for task-relevant features determining downstream LLM performance.
approach: Introduces Feature Activation Coverage measuring diversity in interpretable feature space; uses sparse autoencoder to identify missing features then synthesizes samples.
contribution: Consistently improves data diversity and downstream performance on instruction following, toxicity detection, reward modeling, behavior steering.

problem: Diffusion model sampling requires many steps to achieve small error; complexity bounds for log-concave sampling lack exponential improvement in error.
approach: Presents algorithms achieving δ-error in polylog(1/δ) steps with Õ(δ)-accurate score estimates; complexity Õ(d polylog(1/δ)) under minimal assumptions.
contribution: Exponential improvement over prior results; first polylog(1/δ) sampler for log-concave distributions using only gradient evaluations.

problem: LLM agents deployed on sensitive tasks risk privacy violations from implicitly contextual information without external safeguards.
approach: PrivAct internalizes contextual privacy preservation via multi-agent learning by embedding privacy preferences into each agent's generation behavior.
contribution: Reduces leakage rates by up to 12.32% while maintaining comparable helpfulness; demonstrates generalization and robustness across diverse multi-agent topologies.

problem: Existing SOR methods model ranking deterministically ignoring variability and stochasticity of human attention shifts.
approach: ProbSOR incorporates probabilistic attention via Group Relative Policy Optimization built on vision-language model with new metrics for probabilistic rankings.
contribution: Demonstrates strong performance in salient object ranking; constructs 15,000-sample ProbSOR dataset supporting probabilistic ranking training and evaluation.

problem: Multi-agent protocol selection lacks standardized evaluation; choice of protocol significantly influences system behavior but remains intuition-driven.
approach: ProtocolBench systematically compares protocols on task success, end-to-end latency, message overhead, and robustness; proposes lightweight ProtocolRouter selector.
contribution: Demonstrates 36.5% variation in completion time across protocols; ProtocolRouter reduces Fail-Storm recovery by 18.1% versus best single-protocol baseline.

problem: Long-horizon language agent RL training suffers from credit misattribution where early correct actions penalized by terminal failures and sample inefficiency.
approach: BEACON leverages compositional task structure via milestone-guided credit assignment; applies temporal reward shaping within segments and dual-scale advantage estimation.
contribution: On long-horizon ALFWorld tasks achieves 92.9% success nearly doubling GRPO's 53.5% while improving sample utilization from 23.7% to 82.0%.

problem: Langevin Monte Carlo sampling from high-dimensional distributions requires many iterations; existing Runge-Kutta LMC requires three gradient evaluations per step.
approach: Proposes higher-order Hessian-free stochastic Runge-Kutta LMC of strong order 1.5 requiring only two gradient evaluations; analyzes under log-smooth conditions.
contribution: Derives uniform-in-time convergence rate O(d^1.5 h^1.5) in non-log-concave settings, matching prior work under log-concavity; reduces computational cost.

problem: Implicit in-context learning relies on task-specific alignment limiting generalizability; existing approaches lack structural ICL understanding.
approach: In-Context Routing extracts reusable structural directions emerging during ICL; employs learnable input-conditioned router modulating attention logits.
contribution: Consistently outperforms implicit ICL methods across 12 datasets; demonstrates robust generalization to out-of-domain tasks where task-specific methods struggle.

problem: Math reasoning improvements in LLMs may reflect narrow overfitting rather than broader problem-solving ability with unclear transfer to other domains.
approach: Evaluates 20+ reasoning-tuned models across math, scientific QA, coding, planning, instruction-following; identifies on-policy fine-tuning as key transfer mechanism.
contribution: Shows on-policy RL preserves general-domain structure while off-policy SFT induces representation/output drift; on-policy methods transfer better regardless of training signal.

problem: Workflow optimization via global graph search collapses multi-step failure traces to binary outcomes obscuring recurring failure structure.
approach: Reframes as distributional refinement over Failure Signature Space; CE-Graph maintains counterexample pool, estimates dense failure modes via Propose-and-Verify loop.
contribution: Improves robustness while reducing optimization cost versus workflow-search baselines; suggests reliability emerges from reshaping failure landscapes.

problem: Selecting reasoning data for distillation via full-trajectory scoring fails scaling to long traces from diverse teachers.
approach: Proposes Local Average Log Probability scoring each step via small preceding context window measuring justification by immediate premises rather than global fluency.
contribution: LALP enables selecting best teacher and curating diverse pools; improves accuracy selecting natural solutions by large margin across math, coding, science tasks.

problem: KL-regularized zero-sum Markov games lack algorithms with improved sample efficiency and theoretical benefits despite empirical success in alignment.
approach: OMG and SOMG use best response sampling with optimistic/superoptimistic bonuses; achieve logarithmic regret scaling inversely with regularization strength β.
contribution: Logarithmic regret in T with Õ(√T) traditional regret scaling, achieving β^(-1) dependence showing KL regularization provides theoretical sample advantage.

problem: Large-scale retrieval systems degrade under distributional shifts; retraining retriever or re-embedding corpus prohibitively expensive.
approach: GRAPE leverages LLM-based query rewriting via Grouped Relative Policy Optimization with ranking signals; addresses score inflation via corpus-relative ranking-based reward.
contribution: Consistently improves performance across multilingual, long-form, multimodal benchmarks; average Recall@10 gain of 4.9% without retriever modification.
